stages.name: Supply-side policy and inequality
stages.title: Supply-side policy and inequality
stages.sub: Understand why market-based supply-side policies can worsen inequality, creating a conflict with the goal of equity.

steps.q: A government cuts the top rate of income tax and cuts unemployment benefits, to sharpen work incentives. Who gains most from the tax cut, and who loses most from the benefit cut?
steps.right: High earners gain, low earners lose
steps.wrong: Low earners gain, high earners lose
steps.hint: Think about who pays the top tax rate and who relies on benefits.

steps.q: A government also weakens trade unions and lets a minimum wage fall in real terms, to make the labour market more flexible. Does this push wages at the bottom up or down relative to the top?
steps.hint: Unions and minimum wages mainly protect lower-paid workers.

steps.right: A fairness goal about how income is shared
steps.wrong: A goal about how much total output is produced
steps.hint: Is this about the size of the pie, or how it is split?

steps.q: A government instead wants people to work as hard and productively as possible, even if pay ends up very unequal. What kind of goal is that?
steps.right: A goal about maximising output and effort
steps.wrong: A goal about how fairly income is shared

steps.q: The tax cuts and labour market reforms that sharpen incentives are the same policies that widen the income gap. Can a government get strong incentives and greater income equality from these policies at once?
steps.right: No, pursuing one tends to worsen the other
steps.hint: Look back at what the incentive-boosting policies did to the gap between rich and poor.
